instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of the lentils in a sieve under cold water and pick out any small stones.
Finely chop the onion and both peppers. Peel the carrot and slice it thin. Mince the 4 garlic cloves.
Peel the potato and cut it into 3/4 inch pieces. Halve the 2 tomatoes and grate the cut sides on the large holes of a box grater into a bowl, then throw away the skins.
Slice the 8 oz chorizo into rounds about 1/2 inch thick.
Heat the 2 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium. Add the chorizo and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until the edges brown and the oil turns orange.
Add the onion, the peppers and the carrot. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant. Stir in the 1 tsp paprika and add the grated tomato right after it, so the paprika doesn't burn.
Cook the tomato for about 3 minutes, until it thickens and turns a shade darker.
Add the lentils, the potato, 6 cups of the broth and the bay leaf. Turn the heat up to high and bring it to a boil.
Cover the pot and turn the heat down low. Simmer for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the lentils are soft and a piece of potato breaks when you press it against the side of the pot.
Take out the bay leaf. Stir in the 3/4 tsp salt, the 1/4 tsp pepper and 1 tbsp of the vinegar.
Chop a small handful of the parsley and scatter it over the pot.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt first, then a few more drops of vinegar.
Serve in bowls with the crusty bread.
method_notes: All three read versions use brown lentils with Spanish chorizo, onion, grated tomato and paprika, and simmer them until soft. Spain on a Fork (the lead) browns sliced chorizo first, softens peppers, carrot and onion in its orange oil, cooks paprika and tomato into a quick sofrito, then simmers the lentils with potato and bay and salts only at the end. Spanish Sabores cooks the lentils separately with a ham bone and stirs in a slow sofrito, and Recipes from Europe adds pork ribs and chard. This one follows the lead with a little more lentil for a dinner portion and finishes with a splash of sherry vinegar. It keeps well and is even better the next day, reheated with a splash of water. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for Spanish) has no version, so the first read version leads.
